# Filtering searches by file type in ripgrep

When you search code for a living, half the battle is keeping noise out of
the result set: vendored assets, generated lockfiles, build artifacts, the
occasional binary that snuck into a `dist/` folder. ripgrep's file-type
system gives you a name-based shortcut for this instead of hand-rolling
globs on every invocation. Four flags drive it: `--type`, `--type-not`,
`--type-add`, and `--type-list`.

## `-t`/`--type`: search only matching files

`--type TYPE` (short form `-t`) restricts ripgrep to files matching a named
file type. Instead of writing out a glob every time you want Rust files
only:

```
$ rg 'fn run' -g '*.rs'
```

you write:

```
$ rg 'fn run' --type rust
```

or, attaching the value directly to the short flag, `rg 'fn run' -trust`.
A type is just a name bound to one or more globs — `rust` is `*.rs`, but
`c` expands to `*.[chH]`, `*.[chH].in`, and `*.cats`, and `cpp` covers a
longer list still, so one flag can stand in for a glob you'd otherwise have
to write by hand every time. You can give `--type` more than once
(`-trust -tpy`), and a file matching *any* of the selected types is
searched. Some type names are aliases for the same definition — `py` and
`python` are the same globs, as are `md` and `markdown`.

`--type` supports one special value, `all`: `--type all` behaves as if
every known type (including any you defined with `--type-add`) had been
passed with its own `--type` flag, which puts ripgrep into a whitelist mode
where only recognized files are searched. This is narrower than "search
everything" — a file with no extension, like a shell script with a shebang
but no `.sh` suffix, matches none of ripgrep's type globs, so `--type all`
skips it even though a plain `rg` would search it.

## `-T`/`--type-not`: search everything except a type

`--type-not TYPE` (short form `-T`) is the mirror image: it excludes files
of a type instead of requiring one.

```
$ rg clap --type-not rust
```

or `rg clap -Trust`. `-t` means "include files of this type," `-T` means
"exclude files of this type," and you can mix both on one command line
(`-Trust -tpy` searches Python files while explicitly excluding Rust ones,
for cases where a file could otherwise match more than one type's globs).
`--type-not` also accepts `all`, and does the opposite of `--type all`: it
searches only files that ripgrep's type definitions *don't* recognize —
so a shell script without an extension would be searched, while a `.bash`
file matching the `sh` type would not.

## `--type-list`: seeing what's defined

Since types are just names for globs, you'll want to check what a type
actually expands to before relying on it:

```
$ rg --type-list | rg '^make:'
make: *.mak, *.mk, GNUmakefile, Gnumakefile, Makefile, gnumakefile, makefile
```

Run bare, `--type-list` prints every available type on its own line, each
followed by a colon and a comma-separated list of its globs. This list
reflects ripgrep's built-in types plus anything you've added or cleared
with `--type-add`/`--type-clear` on that same command line — it's a live
view of the current invocation's type table, not a fixed reference.

## `--type-add`: defining your own types

When you find yourself repeating the same glob across searches, define a
type for it:

```
$ rg --type-add 'web:*.{html,css,js}' -tweb title
```

This adds a `web` type matching that glob and immediately searches it for
`title`. Only one glob is added per `--type-add`, but you can repeat the
flag to build up a type from several patterns, and repeated `--type-add`
flags append to any globs a type already has (including ripgrep's built-in
ones) unless you first clear it with `--type-clear TYPE`. You can also
compose a type out of existing ones with the `include:` directive — for
example, `--type-add 'src:include:cpp,py,md'` defines `src` as the union of
the `cpp`, `py`, and `md` types, and you can still add more globs to `src`
with a further `--type-add`. Type names may only contain Unicode letters
and numbers; punctuation isn't allowed.

The important caveat: `--type-add` only affects the invocation it's passed
to. It doesn't persist a new type anywhere. To get a custom type on every
search, either alias the command —

```
alias rg="rg --type-add 'web:*.{html,css,js}'"
```

— or put `--type-add=web:*.{html,css,js}` in a ripgrep configuration file
referenced by the `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable, one flag per
line.

## Where type filtering sits relative to other filters

Type selection is checked after `--glob`/`-g` overrides and after
`.gitignore`/`.ignore` rules, and before nothing else — so an explicit
`--glob` always wins over `--type`/`--type-not`, and a file already
excluded by an ignore file stays excluded regardless of which type it
matches. If a glob-based include or exclude isn't behaving as expected
alongside a `--type` flag, check there first.
